title: QualiZeal Knowledge Fabric - licence manifest (invariant I14: licence-clean)
maintained_by: hand-maintained; validated on every CI run by scripts/licence_gate.py

policy.description: Licences are grouped into classes; each linkage kind lists the classes it may use. 'runtime' means code imported into the shipped Python process; 'optional-runtime' is a guarded import (try/except ImportError) selected by env; 'model-weights' are downloaded artefacts; 'tooling' runs at build/deploy time and never ships; 'external-service' is reached over the network and its code is never linked; 'managed-service' is a cloud-provider service behind an open protocol (S3/SQS-class) with an open-source equivalent listed.

scan.note: Every non-stdlib import found under 'packages' must be declared below with matching import_names; optional-runtime imports must be guarded by try/except ImportError so the shipped process never hard-depends on them.

notes: Copyleft (AGPL MinIO, Grafana, Tempo) is acceptable ONLY as an external service: we talk to it over the network, never import or vendor its code, never ship it in our image.

MPL-2.0 (OpenTofu) is file-level copyleft and acceptable for tooling: we do not modify or redistribute its sources. Tooling in general (GNU Make, OpenTofu) is RUN at build/deploy time and never shipped, so any OSI licence is acceptable there; source-available and proprietary tooling is not.
Proprietary and source-available (SSPL/BUSL/Elastic) components are never approved; they appear here only as rejected alternatives so the decision is on record.
Model weights carry their own licence and are cleared per deployment; only permissive weights (bge-m3 MIT) are pre-approved.

components.name: Python standard library
components.why: The ONLY runtime dependency of the shipped process (sqlite3, hmac, json, http.server, urllib, unittest).

components.name: SQLite (bundled in Python sqlite3)
components.why: Local adapter for every store; tenant filter enforced at the repository layer.

components.name: boto3 / botocore
components.why: Only imported when KF_OBJECTSTORE=s3 / KF_QUEUE=sqs; guarded import raises CloudNotReady when absent.

components.name: pg8000
components.why: Pure-Python driver chosen over psycopg (LGPL-3.0) so the runtime stays permissive-only.

components.name: Docling
components.why: Drop-in behind the DocumentConverter contract for binary PDFs/scans; DoclingLite (native, stdlib) covers text/markdown/csv/transcripts today.

components.name: PostgreSQL
components.why: Managed RDS Postgres in deploy/aws; reached over the network via pg8000.

components.name: pgvector
components.why: Vector search inside Postgres; same tenant-filtered contract as the SQLite vector index.

components.name: MinIO
components.licence_name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
components.why: AGPL: allowed ONLY as an external service spoken to over the S3 protocol. Its code is never imported, vendored or shipped in our image.

components.name: Amazon S3 / SQS / RDS / ECS / Secrets Manager / CloudWatch / Cognito
components.why: Infrastructure behind open protocols (S3 API, OIDC, OTLP); open-source equivalents are MinIO, PostgreSQL, Keycloak. Application code never learns which shape it runs in.

components.name: Keycloak
components.why: Enterprise SSO: the same identity adapter points at the corporate JWKS instead of the local HS256 IdP.

components.name: Dex
components.why: Federating OIDC issuer when Keycloak is too heavy.

components.name: bge-m3 (BAAI)
components.why: GPU-box embedder behind the Embedder contract; the deterministic hashing embedder is the local default (I9: never re-embed on provider swap).

components.name: vLLM
components.why: Serves open weights behind the OpenAI-compatible HostedModelClient (KF_MODEL_BASE_URL); model weights cleared per deployment.

components.name: OpenTelemetry Collector (OTLP/HTTP receiver)
components.why: Receives our OTLP/JSON traces (stdlib urllib POST, no SDK) and fans out to any backend; the app never links the OTel SDK.

components.name: Jaeger
components.why: Permissive trace UI that accepts OTLP directly (Jaeger v2).

components.name: Prometheus
components.why: Scrapes /metrics; optional when the built-in dashboard is enough.

components.name: Grafana
components.licence_name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
components.why: AGPL: external service only, fed by OTLP/Prometheus; the shipped dashboard is our own (knowledge_fabric/surfaces/dashboard.py).

components.name: Grafana Tempo
components.licence_name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
components.why: AGPL: external service only; receives OTLP from the collector.

components.name: OpenTofu
components.why: MPL-2.0 is file-level weak copyleft: acceptable for tooling we run unmodified at deploy time. Chosen over Terraform (BUSL-1.1, source-available).

components.name: Docker Engine (Moby) + python:3.11-slim image
components.licence_name: Apache License 2.0 (Moby); image contents PSF-2.0 + Debian DFSG-free packages
components.why: Single portable image, identical across local / interim / client.

components.name: GNU Make
components.licence_name: GNU General Public License v3.0 or later
components.why: GPL tooling run unmodified; nothing of it ships. Listed for completeness and honesty.

components.name: GitHub Actions runners
components.licence_name: GitHub Terms of Service (service, not software)
components.why: Runs `make ci` (unittest + licence gate + identifier-safety). Any runner that has Python 3.11 works.

components.name: unittest (stdlib) + our own dashboard/surfaces
components.why: No pytest, no charting library: the Power BI-style dashboard is inline SVG served by the platform.

components.name: LangSmith
components.licence_name: LangChain Inc. proprietary terms (SDK MIT, service proprietary + per-seat/per-trace pricing)
components.why: Not needed: the telemetry spine already records one trace per answer with tier, tokens in/out, cost, why, cache savings, model, complexity, per user/role, and exports OTLP. Proprietary licence + trace data leaving the tenant boundary.

components.name: LangFuse
components.licence_name: MIT (core); ee/ directory and Cloud under a commercial licence
components.why: Licence-acceptable (MIT core) but redundant: it would duplicate our spans table, dashboard and curator queue and add a ClickHouse+Postgres+Redis/S3 stack to operate. Revisit only if prompt-versioning UI or human-annotation queues become a product requirement not met by the question bank + curation queue.

components.name: LangChain / LangGraph
components.why: Licence-acceptable but not adopted: the reasoning planner, selector and grounding gate are deterministic, testable stdlib code; a framework would hide the 'why' the roadmap asks us to show.

components.name: Elasticsearch
components.why: Not approved: source-available primary licence. OpenSearch (Apache-2.0) or Postgres full-text are the approved routes if SQLite FTS is outgrown.

components.name: OpenSearch
components.why: Permissive lexical/vector engine if the SQLite/Postgres lexical index is outgrown.

components.name: Terraform (HashiCorp)
components.why: Source-available since 1.6; OpenTofu (MPL-2.0) applies the same HCL modules.

components.name: PyJWT
components.role: OIDC/JWKS token verification (cloud identity adapter, KF_IDENTITY=oidc)
components.why: Verifies RS256/ES256 tokens from Cognito or a corporate IdP; guarded import, fails closed when absent.

components.name: cryptography
components.role: asymmetric signature primitives used by PyJWT for RS256/ES256
components.why: Only present in the cloud-capable image (KF_EXTRAS); never imported directly by application code.
